absent: Layout, size and locking for the per-CPU floating point cache object and its last-state fields.
Numeric encodings of FP_STATE_CURRENT, thread flag numbers, vector length ranges and trap register bits beyond the two EL0 enables.
Implementations and contracts of host capability queries, vector length getters and register access helpers.
Complete dispatch and handling for each exception class beyond the code and field constants shown.
Locking, preemption and context switch rules for the bind operation beyond the return to user serialization note.
Error recovery or fallback behaviour when optional vector state storage is absent.

findings.text: The per-CPU floating point cache is associated with the running thread by recording references to that thread's SIMD state, vector states, vector lengths, streaming mode control, floating point mode and type flag, marking the cached image as current and noting the present CPU. The operation expects host floating point support and, where vector extensions exist, reconciles user trap permissions with the thread flags for those extensions, with final serialization provided by the return to user path.

User execution permission for each vector extension has two states chosen at bind time from the corresponding thread flag. A set flag selects the enabled state that permits direct user execution, while a clear flag selects the disabled state that traps user execution. The choice is reapplied on every bind and only considered when the host reports the extension as present.

User trap control for the vector extensions is configuration dependent. In supporting builds each extension provides a matched enable and disable helper that respectively sets and clears its dedicated EL0 enable field in the host trap control register. In other builds the same helper names are defined to fail compilation, so any reference without support is rejected at build time rather than silently ignored.

Binding the floating point cache without host support is treated as a programming error signalled through a kernel warning check. Using a vector trap helper in a build that lacks the extension is a compile time error, which prevents booting or running with an inconsistent trap configuration.

Interrupt exit consults a predicate that decides whether scheduler preemption is allowed. Preemption is denied when priority masking is in use and the interrupt mask register still shows deferred state indicating NMI handling, and while processor capability finalization is incomplete to avoid resuming stale saved processor state after capability updates. In all other cases preemption is permitted.
The syndrome register header uses a single include guard macro so its exception class codes and field layouts are defined once per compilation unit.

Early exception class values are ESR_ELx_EC_UNKNOWN zero, ESR_ELx_EC_WFx one, ESR_ELx_EC_CP15_32 three, ESR_ELx_EC_CP15_64 four, ESR_ELx_EC_CP14_MR five, ESR_ELx_EC_CP14_LS six, ESR_ELx_EC_FP_ASIMD seven, ESR_ELx_EC_CP10_ID eight restricted to EL2, ESR_ELx_EC_PAC nine usable at EL2 and above, ESR_ELx_EC_OTHER ten, ESR_ELx_EC_CP14_64 twelve, ESR_ELx_EC_BTI thirteen and ESR_ELx_EC_ILL fourteen.

Supervisor call and system trap classes are ESR_ELx_EC_SVC32 seventeen, ESR_ELx_EC_HVC32 eighteen restricted to EL2, ESR_ELx_EC_SMC32 nineteen usable at EL2 and above, ESR_ELx_EC_SVC64 twenty one, ESR_ELx_EC_HVC64 twenty two usable at EL2 and above, ESR_ELx_EC_SMC64 twenty three usable at EL2 and above, ESR_ELx_EC_SYS64 twenty four, ESR_ELx_EC_SVE twenty five, ESR_ELx_EC_ERET twenty six restricted to EL2, ESR_ELx_EC_FPAC twenty eight usable at EL1 and above, ESR_ELx_EC_SME twenty nine, ESR_ELx_EC_IMP_DEF thirty one restricted to EL3, ESR_ELx_EC_IABT_LOW thirty two, ESR_ELx_EC_IABT_CUR thirty three and ESR_ELx_EC_PC_ALIGN thirty four.

Data, debug and fault classes are ESR_ELx_EC_DABT_LOW thirty six, ESR_ELx_EC_DABT_CUR thirty seven, ESR_ELx_EC_SP_ALIGN thirty eight, ESR_ELx_EC_MOPS thirty nine, ESR_ELx_EC_FP_EXC32 forty, ESR_ELx_EC_FP_EXC64 forty four, ESR_ELx_EC_GCS forty five, ESR_ELx_EC_SERROR forty seven, ESR_ELx_EC_BREAKPT_LOW forty eight, ESR_ELx_EC_BREAKPT_CUR forty nine, ESR_ELx_EC_SOFTSTP_LOW fifty, ESR_ELx_EC_SOFTSTP_CUR fifty one, ESR_ELx_EC_WATCHPT_LOW fifty two, ESR_ELx_EC_WATCHPT_CUR fifty three, ESR_ELx_EC_BKPT32 fifty six, ESR_ELx_EC_VECTOR32 fifty eight restricted to EL2 and ESR_ELx_EC_BRK64 sixty.

The syndrome register holds a six bit class starting at bit twenty six with largest value sixty three, an instruction length flag at bit twenty five, a low syndrome occupying bits twenty four through zero, and an extended syndrome occupying bits fifty five through thirty two. Dedicated masks isolate each region, with the class and extended syndrome shifted down on extraction and the low syndrome used directly.

Abort qualifier positions are ESR_ELx_WNR at bit six, ESR_ELx_IDS at bit twenty four, ESR_ELx_AET as three bits at ten with ESR_ELx_AET_UC zero, ESR_ELx_AET_UEU one, ESR_ELx_AET_UEO two, ESR_ELx_AET_UER three and ESR_ELx_AET_CE six, ESR_ELx_VNCR at thirteen, ESR_ELx_SET_MASK as two bits at eleven, ESR_ELx_FnV at ten, ESR_ELx_EA at nine and ESR_ELx_S1PTW at seven, each single bit flag occupying its named shift.

Fault status uses ESR_ELx_FSC mask sixty three with ESR_ELx_FSC_TYPE sixty and ESR_ELx_FSC_LEVEL three. Base encodings are ESR_ELx_FSC_EXTABT sixteen, ESR_ELx_FSC_MTE seventeen, ESR_ELx_FSC_SERROR seventeen, ESR_ELx_FSC_ACCESS eight, ESR_ELx_FSC_FAULT four, ESR_ELx_FSC_PERM twelve, ESR_ELx_FSC_SEA_TTW twenty plus level, ESR_ELx_FSC_SECC twenty four, ESR_ELx_FSC_SECC_TTW twenty eight plus level, ESR_ELx_FSC_EXCL_ATOMIC fifty three and ESR_ELx_FSC_ADDRSZ zero. Level variants add the level to the base, with ESR_ELx_FSC_FAULT_nL forty four used for negative levels, ESR_ELx_FSC_ADDRSZ_nL yielding forty one for minus one and forty four otherwise, and the level helpers selecting the negative form when the level is below zero.

Data abort syndrome positions are ESR_ELx_ISV at twenty four, ESR_ELx_SAS as two bits at twenty two, ESR_ELx_SSE at twenty one, ESR_ELx_SRT_MASK as five bits at sixteen, ESR_ELx_SF at fifteen, ESR_ELx_AR at fourteen, ESR_ELx_CM at eight, ESR_ELx_HDBSSF at eleven, ESR_ELx_TnD at ten, ESR_ELx_TagAccess at nine, ESR_ELx_GCS at eight, ESR_ELx_Overlay at six, ESR_ELx_DirtyBit at five and ESR_ELx_Xs_MASK as five bits at zero.

Condition and wait syndromes use ESR_ELx_CV at twenty four, ESR_ELx_COND_MASK as four bits at twenty, ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_RN as five bits at five, ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_RV at two, ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_TI as two bits at zero with ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_WFI zero, ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_WFE one and ESR_ELx_WFx_ISS_WFxT two, plus ESR_ELx_xVC_IMM_MASK covering sixteen bits. Other trap codes are ESR_ELx_ISS_OTHER_ST64BV zero, ESR_ELx_ISS_OTHER_ST64BV0 one, ESR_ELx_ISS_OTHER_LDST64B two, ESR_ELx_ISS_OTHER_TSBCSYNC three and ESR_ELx_ISS_OTHER_PSBCSYNC four. DISR_EL1_IDS is bit twenty four, DISR_EL1_ESR_MASK combines async error with external abort and fault status, ESR_ELx_WFx_MASK pairs the class mask with trap bits excluding the timed encoding with ESR_ELx_WFx_WFI_VAL as its WFI matcher, and ESR_ELx_BRK64_ISS_COMMENT_MASK covers sixteen bits.

Sixty four bit system trap syndrome uses ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_RES0_SHIFT twenty two with a three bit mask, direction in bit zero with read one and write zero, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_RT_SHIFT five with a five bit mask, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_SHIFT one with four bits, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRN_SHIFT ten with four bits, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_OP1_SHIFT fourteen with three bits, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_OP2_SHIFT seventeen with three bits and ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_OP0_SHIFT twenty with two bits, plus joined system and operation masks, a five field constructor and a target register extractor.

Cache maintenance CRM values are ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_DC_CIVAC fourteen, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_DC_CVADP thirteen, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_DC_CVAP twelve, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_DC_CVAU eleven, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_DC_CVAC ten and ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_CRM_IC_IVAU five, with an EL0 operation mask joining encoding plus direction and a value for op zero one op one three op two one CRN seven CRM zero with write direction. MRS matching uses a mask over OP0 OP1 CRN and direction with a value for op zero three with read direction. Timer and ID values are ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_SYS_CTR for three three one zero zero, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_SYS_CNTVCT for three three two fourteen zero, ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_SYS_CNTVCTSS for three three six fourteen zero and ESR_ELx_SYS64_ISS_SYS_CNTFRQ for three three zero fourteen zero, each combined with read direction where noted, plus converters that rebuild a system register encoding from the syndrome fields with fixed op zero three for the CP15 form.

Return trap codes are ESR_ELx_ERET_ISS_ERET two and ESR_ELx_ERET_ISS_ERETA one, and ESR_ELx_FP_EXC_TFV is bit twenty three. Thirty two bit CP15 syndrome mirrors the sixty four bit layout with direction in bit zero, target at five, CRM at one, CRN at ten, OP1 at fourteen and OP2 at seventeen, plus a mask and constructor over those fields. Sixty four bit CP15 syndrome uses target at five, second target at ten, four bit OP1 at sixteen and CRM at one with its own mask and constructor. Timer specializations are CNTVCT for op one one CRM fourteen, CNTVCTSS for op one nine CRM fourteen and CNTFRQ for op one zero op two zero CRN fourteen CRM zero, each with read direction.

SME trap reason occupies bits two through zero with ESR_ELx_SME_ISS_SMTC_SME_DISABLED zero, ESR_ELx_SME_ISS_SMTC_ILL one, ESR_ELx_SME_ISS_SMTC_SM_DISABLED two, ESR_ELx_SME_ISS_SMTC_ZA_DISABLED three and ESR_ELx_SME_ISS_SMTC_ZT_DISABLED four, extracted by masking the low three bits. Memory operation syndrome uses ESR_ELx_MOPS_ISS_MEM_INST at twenty four, ESR_ELx_MOPS_ISS_FROM_EPILOGUE at eighteen, ESR_ELx_MOPS_ISS_WRONG_OPTION at seventeen, ESR_ELx_MOPS_ISS_OPTION_A at sixteen and three five bit register numbers at ten, five and zero for destination, source and size.
